title: Specified point-transport cone comparison and descent through roofs
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum $p,a,q,k_0,k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, a uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\ge1$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $g=\operatorname{Spec}(\gamma)$ for geometric Frobenius [def-weil-frobenius-detailed], $R=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}=\lim_n(A_n)_s$, and $\Gamma=\Gamma(s,-)$ on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. For a flat-term K-flat complex $P$ of $R$-modules [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], put $P_n=P\otimes_R(A_n)_s$, $r_n(x)=x\otimes1$, and $t_n=1\otimes(A_{n+1}\to A_n)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $C_n=\operatorname{Res}_ng_n^*P_n$, with the coefficient-induced transition $v_n:C_{n+1}\to C_n$ of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b); put $D_n=\Gamma P_n$, $B_n=\Gamma C_n$. All these towers are over the single integral coefficient ring after restriction of scalars. For a strict tower $X_\bullet$ with transitions $w_n$ set $s_X((x_n)_n)=(w_nx_{n+1})_n$ and $H(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_X)[-1]$, with $H(X)^i=\prod_nX_n^{i-1}\oplus\prod_nX_n^i$ and $d(b,a)=(-db-(1-s_X)a,da)$ [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]. Let $N$ be a complex of $R$-modules and $q:P\to N$ a quasi-isomorphism. Use $\sigma$ of [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport] and $\theta_n=\kappa_{P_n}g^{-1}(r_n)$ of comparison (b) [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison]. Suppose $u:D_\bullet\to B_\bullet$ is a strict tower map satisfying $\Gamma(\theta_n)\sigma_P=u_n\Gamma(r_n)$ for every $n$. Put $a_P(z)=(0,(\Gamma(r_n)z)_n)$ and $\widetilde\theta_P(w)=(0,(\theta_nw)_n)$; let $c_C:\Gamma H(C_\bullet)\to H(B_\bullet)$ be the identity on the two sectionwise product components. Then the following is a chain-map equality, including the shifted-product component:
$$c_C\Gamma(\widetilde\theta_P)\sigma_P=H(u)a_P.$$
Use the ambient completed pullback $Lg^*$ on $D(s_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E)$ of [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], whose restriction to integral constructible objects is [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Under its specified representative comparison identifying $Lg^*N$ with $H(C_\bullet)$, let $b_q:\Gamma Lg^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}H(B_\bullet)$ be induced by $c_C$. The specified integral comparison $\kappa_N=[\widetilde\theta_P][g^{-1}q]^{-1}$ and $\iota_N=\Gamma(\kappa_N)\sigma_N$ satisfy
$$b_q\iota_N\Gamma(q)=[H(u)a_P],\qquad b_q\iota_N=[H(u)a_P][\Gamma(q)]^{-1}.$$
Here exact sections make $\Gamma(q)$ invertible, and $\sigma_N\Gamma(q)=\Gamma(g^{-1}q)\sigma_P$. These identities compare the actual integral map of part (b), including its zero shifted-product component. If the family $u(P)$ commutes with chain maps between flat-term K-flat representatives, these identities are independent of those representatives under the specified completed-pullback comparison maps and are natural for arbitrary derived morphisms: for any roof $P\xleftarrow{a}Q\xrightarrow{b}P'$ with $a$ a quasi-isomorphism in that resolving class they commute with $[b][a]^{-1}$. No derived-completeness hypothesis on $[N]$ and no invertibility of $[a_P][\Gamma(q)]^{-1}$ is required.

proof.text: The two reduction presentations are definitionally identical. For every complex P, apply [lem-trf-strict-quotient-unit-compatible], then the section-complex functor. After each product projection the reduction tuple composed with one minus shift is the nth unit minus the next unit followed by transition, hence zero. This proves augmentation_condition and constructs the specified zero shifted-coordinate lift without any goodness assumption.

The mapping-cocone lift equations and product projection equations give both coordinates of augmentation and, directly from the construction in [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison], both coordinates of inverseImageRoosComparisonComplex. The normalized section comparison of [lem-trf-completed-stalk-reparametrization-coherence] and the diagonal Roos-map formulas reduce the unshifted coordinate equality to hv, and both shifted coordinates to zero. Product projections and the two cocone projections jointly determine a chain map. No clause of the separate cone-lifts-and-chain-naturality statement is needed. The proved generic Roos-map coordinate API of [lem-trf-point-quotient-augmentation-diagram] and product/cocone extensionality API of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] supply these elementary identities; their larger final comparison packages are not applied.

Apply [lem-trf-point-transport-resolution-cancellation] to q. The representative formula characterizing integral point transport in [def-weil-frobenius-point-transport], at the identity representing isomorphism, identifies its resolution recipe with the specified integral transport. Substitute the strict comparison into the cancellation formula. Multiplication by the invertible derived section map of q gives the other derived identity; the strict sigma square is the cancellation lemma's third clause.

For a good quasi-isomorphism a, its image under the good-complex localization is invertible. The canonical targetComparison of [lem-trf-point-pullback-cone-localization], constructed from integral-operations well-definedness, exact point sections and the sections/Roos comparison, conjugates that image under completed pullback and sections to the actual diagonal sectionwise Roos map. Functors preserve isomorphisms, and Mathlib NatIso.isIso_map_iff proves pullbackRoof_isIso even without the non-characteristic hypothesis.

Reuse the already proved naturalIntegralTransport helper of [lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural], whose components are the specified integral transport. Step 3 supplies its resolution formula. At the identity resolution, representativeComparison_eq identifies b_id with the canonical target comparison of [lem-trf-point-pullback-cone-localization], since all mapped identities are identities. Conjugating the ambient natural transformation by the source and target comparisons therefore gives a natural transformation on good complexes with components exactly coneArrow. No separate reconstruction of chain naturality or ambient descent is needed.

Componentwise equality with the specified transport proves uniqueness of the natural transformation. For two resolutions, compose each formula of step 3 with its representative comparison inverse; both recipes equal that same transport. For the roof identity, apply the naturality square of coneArrow to a and b. Cancel the invertible source map of a, then cancel the target map with its inverse. This gives eta_P followed by T(a) inverse and T(b) equal to S(a) inverse, S(b), eta_Pprime. Identify T(a) inverse with pullbackRoofIso.inv. Only resolution maps and specified comparison isomorphisms are inverted.
